subject: manipulating Effective Strip Width (ESW) values for site-to-site

messages.author: c37835b7e72885a4
messages.subject: manipulating Effective Strip Width (ESW) values for site-to-site
parts:
Hello all,

I have completed initial Distance analysis of transect data for
primates and large frugivorous birds from three tropical forest sites
in Peru. My survey effort at each site was just over 100km, and the
analysis was done on a site-by-site basis, with no pooling or
stratification (as I am looking to compare densities across sites).
As such, the data is a bit sparse for a few species, but nonetheless
exhibits useful trends. My main concern - likely a result of the
limited quantity of data - is that several values for Effective Strip
Width (ESW) generated by Distance (using the Hazard Rate Simple
Polynomial model with R truncation of 5% and L truncation of 1m) are
either lower or higher than expected. The final density estimates
reflect this, and I believe could be improved given a more accurate
estimate of ESW. Variability in ESW values across sites but for the
same species is especially concerning, given that the true ESW values
should be consistent; as all three forest sites have the same basic
composition and forest structure, a given species should be equally
detectable across them all, and thus ideally would have the same ESW
value for all three sites.
I could estimate ESW for each species based on my observations of
their detectability, but I am not sure whether it would be acceptable
or even possible to input these estimated ESW values manually, which
would also alter the final density value. If it is possible and
acceptable to directly manipulate the ESW, how can I do that? If it
is not, is there another approach that I could take which would
otherwise increase or decrease a given ESW value (and consequently the
density estimate as well) to a level that I feel is appropriate, and
consistent across the three sites?
I appreciate any advice or suggestions you might have. If you
have questions in response to my post, I would be happy to elaborate.
Thanks very much for your time!! Sincerely,

Cooper Rosin
